papers_read.title_as_printed: Longitudinal study of early mild cognitive impairment via similarity-constrained group learning and self-attention based SBi-LSTM (Lei et al.; Knowledge-Based Systems 2022)
Regularized spatio-temporal weighted graph convolution network based on multimodal fusion for mild cognitive impairment detection (Wu, Dong, Wu; Expert Syst Appl 2026)

what_each_reports.P-71: ADNI-2 (33 NC, 39 EMCI, 30 LMCI) and ADNI-3 (16 NC, 25 EMCI, 10 LMCI), each subject with baseline and year-1 rs-fMRI; similarity-constrained group sparse networks + self-attention SBi-LSTM, LOOCV. LMCI vs NC on the pooled ADNI-2&3 set, fusion of the two time points: ACC 91.42%, AUC 96.43% (Table 4); 92.06% on ADNI-2 alone (Table 2).
what_each_reports.P-79: ADNI2 (161 NC, 147 EMCI, 128 LMCI), single time point rs-fMRI + T1 gray-matter volume + age/sex population graph, stratified 5-fold CV: NC vs LMCI 97.44% (AUC 99.75%); other tasks 95.39-95.56%, ADNI3 NC vs MCI 87.08%. The '+8.5%' in the abstract is 'an average improvement of 8.5% in accuracy over baseline models'.

quantity_a: LOOCV accuracy of LMCI vs NC from two-time-point (baseline + year 1) rs-fMRI connectivity in 89 pooled ADNI-2/3 subjects.
quantity_b: As recorded: P-79's average accuracy improvement over its own baselines (a margin in percentage points), not an accuracy.
incompatible_if_same: No. The record's gap of 0.829 is 0.9142 minus 0.085, an accuracy set against an improvement margin. On the task-matched figure P-79 does report (NC vs LMCI 97.44%), the two are different methods with different inputs (longitudinal rs-fMRI only vs cross-sectional rs-fMRI + T1 + phenotype) and different validation, and neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match: LMCI vs NC within MCI-spectrum detection (T1).
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI (P-71 ADNI-2/3 with year-1 follow-up; P-79 ADNI2 cross-sectional).
gates.validation_tier: match in tier (internal only): LOOCV vs stratified 5-fold.
gates.modality_family: partial: both rs-fMRI; P-79 adds T1 structural MRI and a demographic population graph; P-71 adds a second time point.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded (accuracy vs relative improvement). Even substituting P-79's 97.44%, the input representation differs (two-time-point functional networks vs single-time-point structure-function fusion).
performance_validity: Not a valid performance comparison as recorded. P-79's NC vs LMCI 97.44% is at or above 0.97 on internal 5-fold CV with no external MCI cohort, so the exclusion would apply if that figure were used.
independence: Distinct author groups; both ADNI, possible subject overlap not stated. (P-71 shares senior authors with P-14, which is not part of this pair.)
grounds: The record's claim_b misreads P-79: '+8.5% vs baseline' is an average improvement over its own baselines, not a classification accuracy, so there is no second result on P-71's quantity.
On the task-matched accuracy P-79 does report (NC vs LMCI 97.44%), the two are different methods on different inputs with no refuted ordering.
That 97.44% would in any case fall under the performance-validity exclusion (at or above 0.97, internal CV only).

evidence_quotes.quote: achieving an average improvement of 8.5% in accuracy over baseline models.
Taking the representative NC vs. LMCI task as an example, the multimodal model achieved an ACC of 97.44%, an AUC of 99.75%, and an F1-score of 97.22%
All subjects have two time-point (baseline and year1) rs-fMRI data with different scan parameters.
Due to the small dataset, the leave one out cross validation (LOOCV) is used in the experiments.
which are from 87.50% to 86.11%, 91.30% to 89.42% and 92.06% to 91.42% in the three detection tasks of EMCI vs. NC, EMCI vs. LMCI and LMCI vs. NC, respectively.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-79: +8.5% vs baseline' treats a relative improvement as a performance result; gap_magnitude 0.829 is computed from unlike quantities.
modality_family 'functional_mri' omits P-79's T1 structural input.

The pack registry lists P-79 Best_Metric 'not reported' although per-task accuracies are printed; P-71's registry Best_Metric 'AUC 0.9261' is the EMCI vs NC fusion AUC on ADNI-2 (Table 2, 92.61), a different task from the LMCI vs NC accuracy the record's claim_a uses.
P-71's 91.42% is the pooled ADNI-2&3 figure (40 LMCI + 49 NC per Table 6), not a single-cohort result; the record does not say so.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing about the record as written; a new candidate on task-matched accuracies would need matched inputs, a refuted ordering, and an external cohort for P-79.
